name: befs_utf2nls
prose: Precondition: sb is a valid BeFS superblock, in points to in_len readable bytes of UTF-8, out and out_len are valid pointers. Postcondition: if BEFS_SB(sb)->nls is NULL it returns -EINVAL without touching *out or *out_len. Otherwise it allocates a buffer of in_len + 1 bytes with kmalloc(GFP_NOFS) into *out; if that fails *out is NULL, *out_len is left unchanged and -ENOMEM is returned. It then converts each UTF-8 character to Unicode and to the NLS charset (uni2char); if any character cannot be decoded, exceeds MAX_WCHAR_T, or cannot be converted it logs an error, frees the buffer (so *out is left dangling and must not be used, *out_len unchanged) and returns -EILSEQ. On success *out points to the NUL-terminated converted string which the caller must kfree, *out_len is set to the number of bytes written (excluding the NUL), and that same count is returned.

name: befs_fh_to_parent
prose: Precondition: sb is a mounted BeFS superblock, fid points to a file handle of fh_len 32-bit words, fh_type is its type. Postcondition: delegates to generic_fh_to_parent with befs_nfs_get_inode as the inode getter. It returns NULL if fh_len <= 2. Otherwise, if fh_type is FILEID_INO32_GEN_PARENT it calls befs_iget(sb, fid->i32.parent_ino) (the generation is ignored) and passes the result to d_obtain_alias: on success it returns a dentry for the parent inode that the caller owns a reference to (released with dput); if befs_iget returns an ERR_PTR (e.g. an invalid or unreadable inode number, including a zero inode number) that ERR_PTR is returned unchanged; if allocating the alias fails it returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM). For any other fh_type no inode is looked up and d_obtain_alias(NULL) yields ERR_PTR(-ESTALE). Never returns NULL except when fh_len <= 2.

name: bm_entry_write
prose: Precondition: file is an open binfmt_misc entry file whose inode->i_private is its Node e; buffer is a user pointer to count readable bytes (count at most 3). Postcondition: parses the command with parse_command. If that returns 1 ('0') it clears the entry's Enabled bit; 2 ('1') sets the Enabled bit; 3 ('-1') takes the root inode lock (inode_lock_nested, I_MUTEX_PARENT), and if the entry is still on the entries list removes it (remove_binfmt_handler: unlinks it under misc->entries_lock and removes its dentry), then releases the root inode lock. In these three cases it returns count (the number of bytes consumed, not the parse_command code). Otherwise (parse_command returned 0 for count == 0, -EINVAL for count > 3 or an unknown command, or -EFAULT if copy_from_user failed) it returns that value unchanged and does nothing else. *ppos is not used or advanced and no reference is taken; the root inode lock is not held on return.

name: btrfs_backref_iter_start
prose: Precondition: iter was set up by btrfs_backref_iter_alloc (iter->fs_info and iter->path valid, path searching the commit root without locking) and bytenr is the logical address of a metadata (tree block) extent. Postcondition: sets iter->bytenr = bytenr and searches the extent tree for the last item with that objectid. If btrfs_search_slot fails it returns that negative errno directly, without releasing the iterator (the path holds whatever the search left). Otherwise on any of these failures it releases the iterator (bytenr, item_ptr, cur_ptr, end_ptr zeroed, path released, cur_key cleared) and returns: -EUCLEAN if the search found an exact key with offset (u64)-1 or landed at slot 0; -ENOENT if the previous item is not an EXTENT_ITEM or METADATA_ITEM for bytenr, or if there is neither an inline backref nor a following keyed backref (TREE_BLOCK_REF or SHARED_BLOCK_REF for bytenr); -ENOTSUPP if the extent item has BTRFS_EXTENT_FLAG_DATA set (data extents are unsupported); or the negative errno of btrfs_next_item. On success it returns 0 with iter->cur_key, item_ptr, cur_ptr and end_ptr set and the path positioned at that item: cur_ptr points just after the btrfs_extent_item header (which, for non-skinny metadata, is the tree block info that precedes the inline refs, or the first inline ref), or, if the extent item has no data after the header, the iterator has been advanced to the first keyed backref item and cur_ptr is its start. No lock or reference is held by the iterator beyond the path.

name: resolve_indirect_refs
prose: Precondition: ctx, path and preftrees are valid; preftrees->indirect holds only indirect refs (none has ref->parent set); sc is NULL or a share-check context. Postcondition: allocates a local ulist of parents (-ENOMEM, nothing changed, if that fails). Then it repeatedly removes the first ref from the indirect tree: refs with count 0 are freed; if sc is set and the ref's root_id differs from sc->root's id the ref is freed and BACKREF_FOUND_SHARED (a positive value) is returned; otherwise resolve_indirect_ref is called. A result of -ENOENT is tolerated: the unresolved ref is moved to the direct tree as is. Any other non-zero result frees the ref and is returned (e.g. -ENOMEM, -EIO, -EUCLEAN, other errors from the tree search). A ref found with parent set is a bug: it returns -EINVAL with a warning. On success each resolved ref receives the first parent found (0 if none) with its inode list, extra prelim_refs are allocated for further parents (-ENOMEM if that fails, after freeing the current ref) and inserted into the direct tree, and the ref itself is then inserted in the direct tree. Returns 0 if the whole indirect tree was consumed. On early return the remaining refs stay in the indirect tree. In all cases the parents ulist and the inode lists it holds are freed.

name: add_delayed_refs
prose: Precondition: fs_info, head (a delayed ref head, normally with head->mutex held by the caller), preftrees and seq are valid; sc is NULL or a share-check context; the caller does not hold head->lock (the function takes and releases it). Postcondition: under head->lock it walks head->ref_tree and ignores refs with node->seq > seq; refs with action ADD_DELAYED_EXTENT or UPDATE_DELAYED_HEAD only trigger a WARN and are skipped; for the others the count is +ref_mod (ADD_DELAYED_REF) or -ref_mod (DROP_DELAYED_REF) and, by ref type, an indirect ref (TREE_BLOCK_REF, EXTENT_DATA_REF) or a direct ref (SHARED_BLOCK_REF, SHARED_DATA_REF) is added to preftrees with GFP_ATOMIC; an unknown ref type only triggers a WARN. An EXTENT_DATA_REF with a negative count and sc set sets sc->have_delayed_delete_refs. A result of BACKREF_FOUND_SHARED from an add call does not stop the loop (it is kept until all delayed refs have been seen), but any other non-zero result stops it immediately. If no error occurred the result is extent_is_shared(sc). It returns 0 on success with no sharing detected, BACKREF_FOUND_SHARED if sharing was found, or the negative errno (e.g. -ENOMEM) of the first failing add call; head->lock is released on every path and no reference is taken.

name: btrfs_delete_unused_bgs
prose: Real function void btrfs_delete_unused_bgs(fs_info) in fs/btrfs/block-group.c (the slice covers only the middle of the loop, so the name is not in the slice; the name field is therefore the real name). Precondition: fs_info is a mounted filesystem; the caller holds no fs_info->reclaim_bgs_lock or unused_bgs_lock. Postcondition: returns nothing. It returns at once, doing nothing, if BTRFS_FS_OPEN is not set, the filesystem is closing, or fs_info->reclaim_bgs_lock cannot be taken with a trylock. Otherwise it takes every block group off fs_info->unused_bgs one at a time; once an error has occurred, or for a mixed space info, a group is only dropped (btrfs_put_block_group). For each remaining group it cancels pending discard work, takes space_info->groups_sem for writing and skips (dropping the list's reference) groups that async discard has not yet fully trimmed (re-queued on the discard list), that are in use, read-only, or the only group of their type, and groups whose space might still be needed (moved to a local retry list). Otherwise it sets the group read-only (an error just skips it), finishes its zone (on -EAGAIN it is put on the retry list), starts a transaction to remove the block group (an error skips it after restoring rw), cleans its pinned extents, bails out and requeues for discard if it reappeared on the discard list, adjusts the space_info pinned/readonly counters, and calls btrfs_remove_chunk; on success with sync discard or a zoned filesystem it moves the group to the transaction's deleted_bgs (taking an extra reference) for discarding at commit; the transaction is ended in every case and the loop reference to the block group is released. If async discard was enabled meanwhile (it was off at entry) it ends the transaction, restores the retry list, punts the unused list to the discard code and returns. Finally the retry list is spliced back to the end of fs_info->unused_bgs and reclaim_bgs_lock is released; all other locks are released on every path.

name: btrfs_create_pending_block_groups
prose: Precondition: trans is a valid transaction handle whose new_bgs list holds block groups created in this transaction that have not yet been fully inserted into the trees. Postcondition: returns nothing and always empties trans->new_bgs, releasing the list's reference on every block group. For each block group in order: if an earlier block group left a non-zero ret the steps below are skipped; otherwise it inserts the block group item (a failure aborts the transaction), then, if BLOCK_GROUP_FLAG_CHUNK_ITEM_INSERTED is not set, adds the chunk item under fs_info->chunk_mutex (failure aborts the transaction), then inserts the device extents (failure aborts the transaction), then calls btrfs_add_block_group_free_space, and adds the sysfs entry for its raid type if missing. These steps are not skipped by a failure of an earlier step for the same block group (only the result of the last attempted step, insert_dev_extents, carries into the next group). In every case it then drops the delayed-refs reservation for the block group insert, removes the block group from the list under unused_bgs_lock, clears BLOCK_GROUP_FLAG_NEW and puts the list reference; if ret is 0 and the group is still unused it is marked unused (btrfs_mark_bg_unused). Finally it releases the transaction's reserved chunk metadata. Failures are reported only through transaction abort, never through a return value.

name: cache_save_setup
prose: Precondition: block_group, trans and path are valid; path is an empty caller-owned path; the caller holds no block_group->lock. Postcondition: returns 0 without touching block_group->disk_cache_state or cache_generation if the SPACE_CACHE mount option is off; returns 0 after setting disk_cache_state = BTRFS_DC_WRITTEN if block_group->length < 100 MiB; returns 0 without touching the state if the transaction is already aborted (this test comes after the length test). On all other paths it computes a state dcs (initially BTRFS_DC_ERROR) and, at the end, always (not conditionally) stores block_group->disk_cache_state = dcs under block_group->lock, and also sets cache_generation = trans->transid when the result is 0 and dcs == BTRFS_DC_SETUP; it also frees the data reservation changeset and releases the path, and drops the inode reference if one was held. Outcomes: the lookup of the free space inode fails with an error other than -ENOENT: returns that error (dcs ERROR); the inode is missing and the block group is read-only: returns 0 with dcs ERROR; otherwise the inode is created (error returned, dcs ERROR) and looked up again (a second miss is a BUG()); updating the inode with generation 0 fails: the transaction is aborted and that error returned (dcs ERROR); the inode already has size and cache_generation == trans->transid: returns 0 with dcs SETUP; truncating a non-empty cache (btrfs_check_trunc_cache_free_space / btrfs_truncate_free_space_cache) fails: its error is returned (dcs ERROR); the group is not BTRFS_CACHE_FINISHED or SPACE_CACHE is off: returns 0 with dcs WRITTEN; BTRFS_TRANS_CACHE_ENOSPC already set on the transaction: returns -ENOSPC (dcs ERROR); btrfs_check_data_free_space failure: its error returned; preallocation success: returns 0 with dcs SETUP; preallocation failure: returns its error, and -ENOSPC additionally sets BTRFS_TRANS_CACHE_ENOSPC in trans->transaction->flags. May create or truncate the free space inode; the caller keeps ownership of trans and path.

name: radix_sort
prose: Precondition: array and array_buf each point to at least num valid struct bucket_item entries (array_buf is scratch of the same size), num >= 1 (array[0].count is read unconditionally) and the maximum count in array is nonzero (ilog2 of 0 is undefined). Postcondition: returns nothing; array_buf is overwritten with intermediate results (contents unspecified on return) and the entries of array are rearranged (a permutation of the same items, no entry lost or duplicated) by a stable LSD radix sort using 4-bit digits (two passes per loop iteration, ending back in array) over the low bitlen bits of count, where bitlen = ALIGN(ilog2(max count), 8), with digits inverted so larger values come first. It sorts by count in non-increasing order only up to those bitlen bits: entries are ordered by count mod 2^bitlen, and the bits at position bitlen and above are not examined, so the result is fully sorted only if every count is below 2^bitlen; in particular when the maximum count is 1 (bitlen 0) no pass runs and array is left unchanged, and a maximum in the range 256-511 leaves bit 8 unsorted. No lock, reference or allocation is involved.

name: push_for_double_split
prose: Precondition: trans, root and path are valid; path->nodes[0] is a write-locked leaf and path->slots[0] the slot where an item needing data_size bytes is to be inserted; path->nodes[1] is write-locked. Postcondition: it first tries push_leaf_right to move the items after the slot into the right sibling; a negative result is returned at once. It then returns 0 if path->slots[0] is 0 or equals the leaf's item count (the slot is at an edge of the leaf), or if the leaf now has at least data_size free bytes. Otherwise it tries push_leaf_left for the items before the slot; a negative result is returned. A push helper returning 1 means 'nothing pushed' (including no space, which is not an error here). The function returns 0 if at least one of the two pushes succeeded (returned 0), and 1 if neither did (the caller must then do a real double split). It never returns 2. A successful push changes the leaf contents and may move path->nodes[0]/slots[0]; the locks held on entry are kept by the path on every return.

name: btrfs_ctree_init
prose: Precondition: called once at module initialisation (__init), before any btrfs_path is allocated. Postcondition: creates the btrfs_path slab cache into btrfs_path_cachep and returns 0 when that succeeds; if the cache cannot be created it returns -ENOMEM and btrfs_path_cachep is NULL. No lock, reference or other memory is held or handed out.

name: btrfs_defrag_file
prose: Precondition: inode, ra (non-NULL, an initialised readahead state for the inode) and range are valid; the caller holds no inode lock (the function takes and releases it per cluster). Postcondition: returns 0 without modifying anything if i_size is 0; returns -EINVAL, also without modifying range, if range->start >= i_size, or if compression is requested (BTRFS_DEFRAG_RANGE_COMPRESS) with a type >= BTRFS_NR_COMPRESS_TYPES or, with the COMPRESS_LEVEL flag, a level invalid for the type. Otherwise it defragments the aligned range in clusters of at most 256 KiB, locking the inode around each: it stops with -EAGAIN if defrag is cancelled, -ETXTBSY (after unlocking) if the inode is a swapfile, quietly (ret unchanged) if the superblock is no longer active, or with the negative result of defrag_one_cluster; defrag_one_cluster returning a positive value (the max_to_defrag limit was reached) ends the loop with ret 0. After the loop range->start is set to the offset reached (cur), so a later call can continue from there. If some sectors were defragged it flushes the mapping when BTRFS_DEFRAG_RANGE_START_IO is set, may set the COMPRESS_LZO or COMPRESS_ZSTD incompat feature according to range->compress_type, and returns the number of sectors defragged (this overrides any error recorded by the loop); otherwise it returns 0 or the negative error from the loop. If compression or no-compression was requested, inode->defrag_compress is reset to BTRFS_COMPRESS_NONE under the inode lock before returning (this lock/unlock pair is only taken in that case). It may lower the mapping's writeback_index to the start of the range. No lock is held on return.

name: btrfs_defrag_root
prose: Precondition: root is a valid btrfs_root with a valid fs_info; the caller holds no transaction on it. Postcondition: if BTRFS_ROOT_DEFRAG_RUNNING was already set (another defrag of this root is running) it returns 0 without doing anything and leaves the bit set. Otherwise this call owns the bit and loops: each pass starts a transaction (a start failure ends the loop with that negative errno), runs btrfs_defrag_leaves on the root, ends the transaction and balances dirty btree pages; the loop ends when the filesystem is closing or when btrfs_defrag_leaves returned anything but -EAGAIN, and also, if it returned -EAGAIN, when defrag has been cancelled (then the result is -EAGAIN). The return value is the last result: 0 when the whole tree was defragmented, the negative errno of the transaction start or of btrfs_defrag_leaves, or -EAGAIN when the work was interrupted by unmount or cancellation. On every path that took ownership, BTRFS_ROOT_DEFRAG_RUNNING is cleared before returning; no transaction, lock or reference is held on return.

name: btrfs_delayed_delete_inode_ref
prose: Precondition: inode is a valid btrfs inode (with i_nlink == 1, the case this is used for) and the caller does not hold the delayed node's mutex. Postcondition: returns -EAGAIN, with no side effect, if BTRFS_FS_LOG_RECOVERING is set; returns PTR_ERR of btrfs_get_or_create_delayed_node if that fails, with no side effect; otherwise it takes a reference on the inode's delayed node and its mutex and returns 0. If BTRFS_DELAYED_NODE_DEL_IREF was not yet set it sets it, increments delayed_node->count and the delayed_root items counter once each; if the bit was already set nothing is changed (the 0 return is the same). The mutex is released and the delayed node reference dropped before returning. No space is reserved.

name: btrfs_run_dev_replace
prose: Precondition: trans is a valid transaction handle of a filesystem with an initialised dev_replace state; called from the transaction commit; the caller does not hold dev_replace->rwsem. Postcondition: takes dev_replace->rwsem for reading to check the state; if dev_replace->is_valid is false or item_needs_writeback is 0 it returns 0 without changing anything. Otherwise it searches the device tree for the BTRFS_DEV_REPLACE_KEY item: -ENOMEM if the path cannot be allocated, or the negative errno of btrfs_search_slot (with a warning) are returned with the item and item_needs_writeback unchanged; if an existing item is smaller than the on-disk structure it is deleted (a delete failure is returned with a warning) and a new item inserted (an insert failure is returned with a warning, leaving the old item deleted); if no item exists a new one is inserted. It then takes dev_replace->rwsem for writing, copies the source devid ((u64)-1 if there is none), read mode, state, start/stop times, error counters and cursors from the in-memory state into the item, records cursor_left_last_write_of_item, clears item_needs_writeback and releases the semaphore. Returns 0 on success in every case (including after inserting a new item, because the insert returns 0). No lock is held on return and the path is freed.

name: run_one_delayed_ref
prose: Precondition: trans, href (the ref head), node and extent_op (possibly NULL) describe a delayed ref to be run; insert_reserved is true when the extent was reserved but not yet inserted in the extent tree. Postcondition: if the transaction is already aborted it returns 0 and, when insert_reserved is true, pins the extent (node->bytenr, node->num_bytes) and frees the head's squota reservation. Otherwise it dispatches on node->type: TREE_BLOCK_REF and SHARED_BLOCK_REF to run_delayed_tree_ref, EXTENT_DATA_REF and SHARED_DATA_REF to run_delayed_data_ref, EXTENT_OWNER_REF is a no-op returning 0, and any other type returns -EUCLEAN after logging an error. If the dispatched call (or the type error) returned non-zero and insert_reserved is true the extent is pinned (this function does not itself free the squota reservation on this path; the data-ref handler frees it before returning). A negative result is logged. It returns the result of the handler: 0 on success, or a negative errno.

name: __btrfs_run_delayed_refs
prose: Precondition: trans is a valid transaction handle; min_bytes is the amount of delayed-ref reservation bytes to process before stopping, where 0 means 'run every ready head' (max_count = number of ready heads at entry, min_bytes treated as U64_MAX). The caller holds no delayed-ref head locks. Postcondition: repeatedly selects a ready delayed ref head, merges its refs, runs them with btrfs_run_delayed_refs_for_head and cleans the head up (cleanup_ref_head), accumulating the bytes of released reservation in a local counter, until no ready head remains and the byte or head-count limit is satisfied. A head whose run returns -EAGAIN is skipped and another head selected. Returns 0 on normal completion, which includes the case that the transaction is already aborted (the per-ref handlers then do nothing). It returns the negative errno (e.g. -ENOMEM, -EIO, -EUCLEAN, or any error from the ref handlers) as soon as running a head or cleaning it up fails; in that case the helper has already unlocked the head and the failing handler or its callers abort the transaction. The accumulated reservation bytes are not returned to the caller (only used for the min_bytes test). No head lock is held on return.

name: __btrfs_free_extent
prose: Real function __btrfs_free_extent(trans, href, node, extent_op) in fs/btrfs/extent-tree.c (the slice starts after the head and the variable set-up). Precondition: trans is a live transaction; href is the ref head, node a delayed ref being dropped (refs_to_drop = node->ref_mod, bytenr and num_bytes from node); extent_op may be NULL; the caller holds the delayed ref head lock. Postcondition: allocates a scratch path (freed automatically on every return) and returns -ENOMEM if that fails. For a tree block (owner_objectid below BTRFS_FIRST_FREE_OBJECTID) with refs_to_drop != 1 it aborts the transaction and returns -EINVAL. It locates the backref with lookup_extent_backref: -ENOENT (with a warning and dump) and any other error from it are returned with the transaction aborted or dumped. It then finds the EXTENT_ITEM/METADATA_ITEM (quick path nearby, otherwise by a second search, trying the non-skinny form too); a failure to find it with a search error aborts and returns that error; inconsistencies on disk (too-small extent item, refs smaller than refs_to_drop, an inline ref without an extent item, a mismatched data ref count, a misplaced inline ref or SHARED_* item) abort or dump the transaction and return -EUCLEAN. If refs remain after the drop it applies extent_op to the extent item, lowers the reference count (or leaves it to remove_extent_backref for an inline ref) and removes the backref via remove_extent_backref (an error aborts and is returned). If the count reaches zero it deletes the extent item together with the adjacent SHARED_* item when there is no inline ref (btrfs_del_items; an error aborts and is returned), releases the path and returns the result of do_free_extent_accounting for the freed extent with a squota delta (for data, the owning root is looked up from the extent owner ref). On success it returns 0 (or the accounting result). Errors may return without btrfs_release_path, but the path is freed by the auto-free.

name: do_allocation_clustered
prose: Precondition: block_group, ffe_ctl and bg_ret are valid for an allocation attempt in find_free_extent; the caller does not hold last_ptr->refill_lock. Postcondition: returns only 0 or 1 (a -ENOENT from find_free_extent_clustered means 'fall back to unclustered mode' and is handled internally by calling find_free_extent_unclustered). If ffe_ctl->last_ptr and ffe_ctl->use_cluster are set it first calls find_free_extent_clustered; a non-negative result of that is returned. Returns 0 when space was found: ffe_ctl->found_offset is set; if the space came from the existing cluster, *bg_ret is set to the cluster's block group (which may be block_group itself; when it is a different group the caller also owns an extra reference on it and, for delalloc, a read hold on its data_rwsem, to be released with btrfs_release_block_group); if a new cluster was set up in block_group or the unclustered search succeeded, *bg_ret is left unchanged. Returns 1 when nothing suitable was found (clustered search failed, or the unclustered search found no space); in that case last_ptr->refill_lock has been released and any reference or data_rwsem hold taken on another block group has been dropped. The unclustered path may mark last_ptr as fragmented and update ffe_ctl->total_free_space and max_extent_size.

name: find_free_extent_update_loop
prose: Precondition: fs_info, ins (the result of the latest search: ins->objectid != 0 means an extent was found), ffe_ctl (loop phase, raid index, caching and empty_size/empty_cluster state), space_info and full_search describe the current find_free_extent state; if the chunk-allocation phase is reached the caller either already has a transaction in current->journal_info or the function joins one on fs_info->chunk_root and ends it again. Postcondition: records orig_have_caching_bg when the first non-waiting caching pass saw an uncached group. Returns 0 if ins->objectid is non-zero (after found_extent(ffe_ctl, ins) records the result). Otherwise returns 1 (caller must search again) if the loop phase is at least LOOP_CACHING_WAIT and a caching block group is pending, or after advancing ffe_ctl->index to the next raid type that is still below BTRFS_NR_RAID_TYPES, or after resetting index to 0 and advancing ffe_ctl->loop (skipping LOOP_CACHING_WAIT when there was no uncached group and a full search was done); when the new phase is LOOP_ALLOC_CHUNK it first calls can_allocate_chunk (a non-zero result is returned), joins a transaction if none (a join failure returns PTR_ERR(trans)), forces a chunk allocation (-ENOSPC is tolerated, advancing the loop again; any other negative error aborts the transaction and is returned) and ends the transaction it joined; when the new phase is LOOP_NO_EMPTY_SIZE it returns -ENOSPC for a non-clustered policy or if empty_size and empty_cluster are already 0, otherwise zeroes empty_size and empty_cluster. Returns -ENOSPC when the loop phase has already reached LOOP_NO_EMPTY_SIZE or beyond and nothing was found. Any joined transaction is ended before returning.

name: find_free_extent
prose: Real function find_free_extent(root, ins, ffe_ctl) in fs/btrfs/extent-tree.c (slice starts mid-function). Precondition: ffe_ctl holds the request (flags, num_bytes, ram_bytes, min_alloc_size, empty_size, hint_byte, delalloc, for_treelog, for_data_reloc); ins is a key the function may write; the caller holds no space_info->groups_sem. Postcondition: it initialises the search state in ffe_ctl, sets ins->type = BTRFS_EXTENT_ITEM_KEY and ins->objectid = ins->offset = 0, finds the space_info for ffe_ctl->flags (a dedicated sub-group for relocation or tree-log on zoned filesystems) and returns -ENOSPC if there is none, returns any negative result of prepare_allocation (for the clustered policy this is -ENOSPC with ins->offset = space_info->max_extent_size when the request is larger than the known largest hole), then iterates the block groups (first the hinted one, then by raid index with repeated passes driven by find_free_extent_update_loop, which may wait for caching and allocate a new chunk) trying clustered or zoned/unclustered allocation. On success it returns 0 with ins->objectid = the start of the allocated extent and ins->offset = ffe_ctl->num_bytes, its bytes added to the block group's reservations (btrfs_add_reserved_bytes) and the block group's reservation count incremented; unused space before the aligned start or beyond a group is returned to the free space. On failure it returns a negative errno: -ENOSPC when no extent was found, in which case ins->offset is set to the largest hole seen (max_extent_size, or total_free_space if no hole was recorded) and space_info->max_extent_size is updated under space_info->lock; but if any block group failed to cache (an error from btrfs_cache_block_group, or -EIO for a group in CACHE_ERROR) that error is returned instead of -ENOSPC; or an error propagated from the update-loop (chunk allocation, joining a transaction). The space_info->groups_sem read lock and every block group reference or data_rwsem hold taken inside are released before return.

name: visit_node_for_delete
prose: Precondition: wc->level > 0 and wc->refs[wc->level - 1] > 0 (asserted); eb is the parent extent buffer being visited (readable, not modified, and not required to be locked by this function), slot a valid pointer slot in it, flags the extent flags of the child at wc->level - 1, and the root and walk control come from a snapshot deletion (sanity checking of the blocks read so far is assumed). Postcondition: pure decision function, returns a bool and changes nothing. If wc->stage == UPDATE_BACKREF it returns false only when wc->level == 1 and flags has BTRFS_BLOCK_FLAG_FULL_BACKREF, otherwise true. In the other stage (DROP_REFERENCE) it returns true if wc->refs[level - 1] == 1 (last reference: must walk into the child); otherwise false if level == 1 and flags has FULL_BACKREF; otherwise false if wc->update_ref is zero or the child's generation (btrfs_node_ptr_generation(eb, slot)) is <= the root's origin generation; otherwise false if the child's key at slot compares below wc->update_progress (already processed by an earlier run); otherwise true.

name: btrfs_split_extent_map
prose: Real function btrfs_split_extent_map(inode, start, len, pre, new_logical) in fs/btrfs/extent_map.c (slice starts after the head, so the name is not in the slice). Precondition: 0 < pre < len; the inode's extent map tree holds a pinned, uncompressed, non-logging extent map exactly covering [start, start + len) with a real disk_bytenr; the caller holds neither the io_tree extent lock on that range nor em_tree->lock. Postcondition: returns -ENOMEM, with nothing locked or changed, if either of the two new extent maps cannot be allocated; otherwise it locks the range in inode->io_tree and takes em_tree->lock for writing, and if no extent map is found for [start, start + len) returns -EIO leaving the tree unchanged. On success it returns 0 after replacing the old map by two maps carrying the old map's flags (including PINNED) and generation: [start, start + pre) mapped to new_logical, and [start + pre, start + len) mapped to the old block start plus pre; the old extent map's tree reference and the caller's lookup reference are dropped. In every case it releases the write lock and the range lock and frees any unused allocated extent maps.

name: emit_fiemap_extent
prose: Precondition: fieinfo, cache (holding at most one cached extent when cache->cached is true, plus the entries[] array of size entries_size), and a new extent (offset, phys, len, flags) not carrying FIEMAP_EXTENT_LAST; the extents are presented in increasing offset order, possibly overlapping the cached one after a re-search. Postcondition: it either merges, replaces, trims or stores the new extent against the cached one and returns 0 or a positive code. If nothing is cached, or the new extent starts exactly at the cached offset, the cache is replaced by the new extent and 0 returned. If the new extent starts inside the cached range, the cached length is cut to end at offset and the cached extent is stored. If it starts before the cached offset, it is ignored (0 returned) when it ends at or before the cached end, otherwise its part past the cached end is kept (offset moved to the cached end, phys advanced unless the extent is encoded or delalloc) and the cached extent is stored. If it is contiguous in logical and physical address with the same flags the cached length is grown and 0 returned. Storing the cached extent appends it to cache->entries (entries_pos and extents_mapped incremented); if entries[] is already full it instead sets cache->next_search_offset to the end of the last stored entry, sets cache->cached = false and returns BTRFS_FIEMAP_FLUSH_CACHE without recording the cached or new extent (the caller must flush and re-search); if after storing, extents_mapped == fieinfo->fi_extents_max, it sets cache->cached = false and returns 1 without caching the new extent. Otherwise the new extent becomes the cached one (cache->cached = true) and 0 is returned. No lock is taken.

name: btrfs_sync_file
prose: Real function btrfs_sync_file(file, start, end, datasync) in fs/btrfs/file.c (slice starts after the head, so the name is not in the slice). Precondition: file is an open btrfs file; the caller holds no btrfs transaction; if current->journal_info == BTRFS_TRANS_DIO_WRITE_STUB (called from a direct-IO write) the inode lock is already held by the caller, the stub is reset to NULL and only the inode's i_mmap_lock is taken here, otherwise the function takes the inode lock with BTRFS_ILOCK_MMAP. Postcondition: the start and end arguments are ignored (the whole file, 0 to LLONG_MAX, is always synced) and datasync only affects tracing. It starts ordered writeback, waits for data (and the ordered extents when the inode needs a full sync, the filesystem is zoned, or a COW write error was recorded). If there is nothing to log it clears BTRFS_INODE_NEEDS_FULL_SYNC and reports only the file's writeback error state. Otherwise it starts a transaction, logs the inode (a logging failure is turned into BTRFS_LOG_FORCE_COMMIT), drops the inode/mmap lock, and: if no log sync is needed (BTRFS_NO_LOG_SYNC) it ends the transaction; if the log sync succeeds it ends the transaction; else (log error or sync failure) it commits the whole transaction, first (for a non-full sync) ending the transaction, waiting for ordered extents and attaching a barrier transaction (-ENOENT from that attach becomes success). It returns 0 on success; the first error otherwise (from ordered writeback, waiting, starting or committing the transaction, or the log sync); if the result is 0 it returns the file's pending writeback error (file_check_and_advance_wb_err); any positive result is returned as -EIO. All locks, the transaction handle, the scratch extent buffer and log-context extent references taken are released before returning.

name: btrfs_replace_file_extents
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the inode lock and has locked the file range [start, end]; path is a usable (empty) path in the inode's root; extent_info is NULL or describes the replacement extent; trans_out is a valid output pointer. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL, changing nothing, if end <= start. Otherwise it starts a transaction with a temporary metadata reservation and drops every file extent overlapping [start, end], possibly over several transactions: when the extent drop runs out of space (-ENOSPC) it commits progress (the dropped part is replaced by hole items, for the part below the rounded i_size, when extent_info is NULL, or merely cleared from the extent range map for the part past i_size; or the replacement extent is inserted piecewise when extent_info is given), updates the inode (i_version and, unless extent_info says otherwise, mtime/ctime) and ends the transaction before starting a new one. After the last drop it fills the remainder with holes (below i_size) or clears the range, or inserts the rest of the replacement extent. If extent_info is non-NULL and not a new extent, the inode is marked for a full fsync. Returns 0 on success, with *trans_out set to the live transaction, which the caller must end. On failure it returns a negative errno (from starting the transaction, migrating the block reservation, dropping extents, filling holes, clearing the range, inserting the replacement extent, updating the inode, or finding the next non-hole), aborting the transaction on most of these (except -EOPNOTSUPP from the drop when no new extent is being inserted), ends the transaction itself and leaves *trans_out unset. In all cases the temporary block reservation is released before returning.
